name: Ragi Dosa
cuisine: South Indian (Karnataka and Tamil Nadu millet tiffin; now on many Udupi and "healthy" menus in Mumbai)

ingredients.name: Ragi flour (finger millet flour, nachni atta)
Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ¼ medium onion, very finely chopped (about 3 tbsp)

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or other neutral oil)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 tsp (1 tsp per dosa, incl. greasing)

equipment: Mixing bowl and a whisk or spoon
Measuring cups and spoons (a steel tumbler and a normal teaspoon are fine stand-ins)
Chopping board and knife; a small grater for ginger (none? chop it very finely)
Dosa tawa, cast-iron or non-stick, about 24–26 cm
Small ladle or a ¼-cup measure, to pour the batter
Half an onion or a folded kitchen towel, to wipe the tawa with oil (optional)
A small bowl of water to sprinkle on the tawa to check heat

steps.title: Measure the ragi flour
steps.text: Put 40 g (⅓ cup) ragi flour in a mixing bowl.
steps.visualCue: Fine reddish-brown flour, no lumps
steps.cameraCheck: The ragi flour in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Ragi flour tipped from a cup into a steel bowl.

steps.title: Add rice flour and rava
steps.text: Add 15 g (1½ tbsp) rice flour and 15 g (1½ tbsp) fine rava.
steps.visualCue: White and cream patches on the brown flour
steps.cameraCheck: The three flours in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Two spoonfuls added to the ragi flour.

steps.title: Add salt and cumin
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt and ¼ tsp cumin seeds; stir the dry mix with a spoon.
steps.visualCue: Even colour, cumin seeds spread through
steps.videoShot: A spoon stirring the dry flours.

steps.title: Add the curd
steps.text: Add 2 tbsp (30 g) curd and 50 ml water. Whisk to a thick, smooth paste.
steps.tip: Making a thick paste first and thinning later avoids lumps.
steps.visualCue: No dry lumps; thick like idli batter
steps.cameraCheck: The thick paste on the whisk
steps.videoShot: Whisk working curd into the flour.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Very finely chop ¼ medium onion (30 g).
steps.tip: Big pieces make holes and tear a thin dosa; chop as fine as you can.
steps.visualCue: Tiny pieces, about 3 tbsp
steps.videoShot: Knife chopping onion finely.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics
steps.text: Finely chop ½ small green chilli (2 g), 4–5 curry leaves and 1 tsp coriander leaves; grate ¼-inch ginger (2 g).
steps.visualCue: Fine green flecks and a little ginger pulp
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves sliced into thin ribbons.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Stir the onion, chilli, ginger, curry leaves and coriander into the paste.
steps.visualCue: Green and white flecks spread evenly
steps.videoShot: Chopped greens folded into the batter.

steps.title: Thin the batter
steps.text: Add about 100 ml more water, a little at a time, whisking, until the batter is thin and runny.
steps.tip: Thick batter gives a soft, chewy dosa; thin batter gives the lacy, crisp one.
steps.visualCue: Flows off the ladle in a steady stream, like thin buttermilk (thinner than normal dosa batter)
steps.videoShot: Ladle lifted, batter streaming back into the bowl.

steps.title: Rest the batter
steps.text: Cover and leave the batter for 15 minutes.
steps.visualCue: The rava softens and the batter thickens slightly; the flours settle at the bottom
steps.videoShot: A plate placed over the bowl.

steps.title: Re-adjust the batter
steps.text: Stir from the bottom; add 1–2 tbsp water if it has thickened.
steps.visualCue: Thin and runny again, no sediment at the bottom
steps.cameraCheck: The batter running off the ladle
steps.videoShot: Ladle scraping the bottom of the bowl.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium-high heat.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sizzle and vanish in 2–3 seconds
steps.cameraCheck: Water drops sizzling on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Water sprinkled on the hot tawa, hissing.

steps.title: Grease the tawa
steps.text: Lower to medium. Spread ¼ tsp oil over the tawa with half an onion or a folded towel.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even sheen, no pools
steps.videoShot: Onion half rubbed over the tawa.

steps.title: Stir and pour the first dosa
steps.text: Stir the batter from the bottom. From about 15 cm above, pour one ladle (about 110 ml, half the batter) onto the tawa, starting at the outer edge and moving inwards in circles.
steps.tip: Don't spread it with the ladle like a normal dosa; pour it, as for rava dosa. Fill only large gaps with a little more batter.
steps.visualCue: A lacy circle about 20 cm across with small holes
steps.cameraCheck: The lacy batter on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Batter poured in circles from the edge to the centre.

steps.title: Add oil
steps.text: Drizzle ¾ tsp oil over the dosa and around its edge.
steps.visualCue: Oil sizzles into the holes
steps.videoShot: A spoon drizzling oil.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium without touching.
steps.tip: If you lift it too early it tears; wait until the edges leave the tawa.
steps.visualCue: Top looks dry, colour darkens to deep brown, edges lift and crisp on their own
steps.videoShot: Edges curling up from the tawa.

steps.title: Flip (optional)
steps.text: For a softer dosa, flip and cook the other side; for a crisp one, skip flipping.
steps.visualCue: A few dark spots on the second side
steps.videoShot: Spatula flipping the dosa.

steps.title: Fold and lift
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half and slide it onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: Crisp, lacy, deep brown with green and white flecks
steps.cameraCheck: The folded dosa on the plate
steps.videoShot: Spatula folding and lifting the dosa.

steps.title: Cool the tawa slightly
steps.text: Sprinkle a few drops of water on the tawa and wipe it with a cloth.
steps.tip: A tawa that is too hot makes the batter clump instead of spreading.
steps.visualCue: Water sizzles off; tawa clean
steps.videoShot: Water hissing, then a cloth wipe.

steps.title: Make the second dosa
steps.text: Grease with ¼ tsp oil, stir the batter from the bottom and pour the rest as in step 13.
steps.visualCue: A second lacy circle
steps.cameraCheck: The second dosa on the tawa
steps.videoShot: Second pour from edge to centre.

steps.title: Cook the second dosa
steps.text: Drizzle ¾ tsp oil and cook as in steps 15–17.
steps.visualCue: Crisp edges, deep brown
steps.videoShot: The second dosa folded and placed beside the first.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with 2 tbsp coconut chutney or a bowl of sambar.
steps.visualCue: Crisp, steaming dosas
steps.videoShot: Dosa torn open beside a bowl of chutney.

reasons: a whole-grain millet base gives about 6.4 g fibre and about 195 mg calcium (about 20% of the day) in 2 dosas, with only 2 tsp oil, no frying, no added sugar, low saturated fat and almost no cholesterol, at about 345 kcal. Points off for modest protein (about 7 g; pair with sambar or peanut/dal chutney), moderate sodium (about 610 mg before chutney and sambar) and the refined rava and rice flour that make up about 40% of the flour. Restaurant versions are often brushed generously with ghee or butter, made with more rice and rava than ragi, and served with salty sambar and coconut chutney, so a plate can reach 450–550 kcal.

researchRating.basis: very well reviewed as a healthy home tiffin: Hebbar's Kitchen's instant ragi dosa shows 5/5 from 272 votes, and almost every major Indian recipe site publishes it (Veg Recipes of India, Indian Healthy Recipes, Jeyashri's Kitchen, Tarla Dalal, Yummy Tummy Aarthi 4.15 from 7 votes); Swiggy reported strong growth in millet dish orders, with ragi among the most-searched healthy keywords. Points off because it is valued more as a "healthy swap" than as a favourite, it is less common on Mumbai menus than plain or rava dosa, and its earthy taste and fragile texture are an acquired taste for some. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Batter: fridge-safe in a closed box for 1 day (it sours further because of the curd; stir and add water before use); not suitable for freezing. Cooked dosas: best eaten fresh; fridge for up to 1 day in a closed box, then reheat on a hot tawa for about 1 minute per side (they soften rather than crisp again). Microwave reheating makes them chewy; not recommended.
leftoverRemix: Ragi dosa kothu. Tear leftover dosas into thin strips. In a pan, sauté 2 tbsp chopped onion, 2 tbsp chopped capsicum and ¼ tomato in 1 tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chilli powder, add the strips and a spoon of leftover sambar or a splash of water, and chop and toss with the spatula for 2 minutes, as for kothu parotta; finish with coriander and lemon.
burnOff: about 4.9 km of running (345 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6.9 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 25 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With coconut chutney (about 415 kcal): about 5.9 km running or 8.3 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: ragi, rice flour and wheat rava are grains outside the common vrat rule set (which allows kuttu, rajgira, singhara or samvat flours) and table salt is used.

ekadashi.reason: grains (rice, wheat rava and ragi) are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set.

jain.reason: onion and fresh ginger are root vegetables; drop both and use sonth (see Jain variant).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; a filling, high-fibre millet tiffin that suits sehri with chutney and sambar; moderate salt (about 610 mg sodium for 2 dosas).

jain.reason: onion and fresh ginger are root vegetables; drop both, use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) and gluten-free hing, and use curd set the same day (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: curd is the only animal product; replace 2 tbsp curd with 2 tbsp water and ½ tsp lemon juice (see Vegan variant).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: the recipe has no garlic; skip the onion (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: ragi and rice flour are gluten-free, but the fine rava (sooji) is wheat semolina; swap it for more rice flour (see Gluten-free variant). If you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour.

dairyFree.reason: curd (dahi) is the only dairy; replace it with water and lemon juice (see Dairy-free variant).
